column1: # Agent runs measured on 2026-09-10 — the coding agents that built the
# cars that landed on main that day, including the car that built the
# recorder they are filed into.
# Filed with infra/record-agent-runs.sh (see that file for the door it
# uses and the refusals it makes). These are OBSERVATIONS, not schema:
# they are POSTed through /api/agent-runs, which prices them, writes the
# projection and the outbox event in one transaction, and collapses a
# retry on run_id. Nothing here belongs in a migration.
# WHERE EACH FIELD COMES FROM, AND WHICH ONE IS NOT MEASURED
# total_tokens / tool_calls / duration_ms
#     Measured. Reported by each coding agent when it finished. The
#     token figure is a SINGLE total — the harness reports
#     `subagent_tokens` and no input/output split exists anywhere — so
#     these rows are filed with total_tokens alone and the server leaves
#     usd_micros NULL. That is the honest answer: agent_rate_card prices
#     input and output at different rates ($5.00 vs $25.00 per MTok on
#     opus-5), so a total cannot be priced, and a blended rate would be
#     a fabricated number wearing a measurement's clothes. The roll-up
#     says so out loud: unpriced_runs = 15, total_only_runs = 15.
# branch
#     Read from the system of record: each branch has a gate-run packet
#     from 2026-09-10 (`GET /api/jobs?kind=gate-run`), and four of them
#     are named in 20260910030644's header with the same token and
#     tool-call figures.
# finished_at
#     DERIVED, and an approximation stated as one: it is the instant the
#     branch's gate-run packet was opened, which is the first thing that
#     happens after a builder reports. Accurate to a minute or two. The
#     run's DURATION is exact regardless, because started_at is computed
#     by subtracting the measured duration_ms from this instant — so the
#     interval's length is measured and only its absolute position is
#     approximate. duration_ms is therefore NOT stored anywhere: the
#     server derives duration from the two instants, and a stored copy
#     could disagree with them.
# job_id
#     Resolved at filing time by the script, by matching this branch
#     against the ship-a-change packets. Left NULL when zero or more
#     than one packet matches — a re-railed branch has two, and guessing
#     which one the run belongs to would put a wrong id on the record.
# actor_id
#     THE ONE FIELD NOT READ FROM THE SYSTEM OF RECORD. Nothing in the
#     packets, the gate runs or the receipts names the model a builder
#     ran as. The basis for `claude:opus-5[1m]` is that these agents
#     were dispatched from the dev pod session, which runs Opus 5 with
#     the 1M context, and a dispatched agent inherits its parent's model
#     unless the dispatch names another — none did. It is stated here as
#     a column rather than defaulted in code so that correcting it is a
#     one-column edit, and so that a night with mixed models can say so.
#     Pricing does not depend on it for these rows: a total-only run is
#     unpriced whatever model ran.
# outcome
#     `success` for all fifteen: every run finished and produced the
#     branch named beside it. This is the AGENT's outcome, not the
#     gate's verdict — those are different facts, and the gate's lives
#     on the gate-run packet.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   run_id  actor_id  branch  total_tokens  tool_calls  duration_ms  finished_at  outcome  label
